name: Teamtailor
tagline: Applicant tracking system with a hosted careers site, job posting distribution, and a collaborative hiring pipeline.

pricing.basis: quote based, scales with company size
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanical core of an ATS is a form, a database, a kanban board, and some email templates, and an agent will hand you all of that in a sitting. Where it breaks down is everything that touches the outside world: syndicating a job to the big boards, hosted careers pages that marketing can edit, interview scheduling against real calendars, and hiring managers who need logins and comment threads. Candidate data also drags compliance along with it, so consent records, retention windows, and deletion requests stop being a nice-to-have the moment you store a real resume. If you are one person hiring two people, the DIY version is genuinely fine and arguably faster. If you are a company with a hiring team and a brand to present, you are rebuilding a product, not a weekend tool.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted careers page with per-role application forms that drop candidates into a kanban pipeline with notes, stage emails, and resume storage.
requirements: SMTP or a transactional email key for candidate notifications
Somewhere to host the public careers page
Disk or object storage for resume uploads
A privacy policy and a retention plan if you keep real candidate data
whatYouLose: One-click distribution to job boards and aggregators, so every role gets posted manually everywhere
Hosted, editable careers pages that non-technical people can change without touching your repo
Interview scheduling that actually talks to Google or Outlook calendars
Multi-user hiring teams: roles, scorecards, comment threads, and who-saw-what
GDPR plumbing: consent capture, automatic retention expiry, and defensible deletion on request
moatNotes: The database half is trivial. The job board connectors, calendar OAuth, and candidate data compliance are the actual product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Hiring is a process with other people in it. Recruiters, hiring managers, and interviewers all need an opinionated shared surface, and candidates judge you by the careers page before they judge you by the job. Paying also outsources the boring risk: resumes are personal data, and a vendor with a DPA and a retention policy is cheaper than discovering yours by accident. A solo founder hiring their first contractor does not need any of that, which is exactly why the DIY build is defensible at small scale and indefensible at thirty employees.
notes: Great one-person hiring tracker, mediocre company hiring system. The gap is job board distribution and other humans having accounts.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted applicant tracking tool for a small team hiring a handful of roles.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript), SQLite via better-sqlite3, Tailwind, Zod for validation. Run it with `npm run dev` on localhost. No external accounts beyond SMTP.

Data model: Job (title, slug, location, employment type, markdown description, status open/closed), Candidate (name, email, phone, resume file path, cover note, source, jobId, stage, createdAt), Note (candidateId, body, createdAt), EmailLog (candidateId, template, sentAt).

Public side:
- /jobs lists open jobs, /jobs/[slug] renders the markdown description plus an application form.
- Application form: name, email, phone optional, cover note, resume upload (pdf/doc/docx, 10MB cap, stored in ./uploads which is gitignored).
- On submit: create the candidate in stage "applied", send a confirmation email, show a plain thank-you page.
- A required consent checkbox that records consentAt, plus a static /privacy page I can edit.

Admin side at /admin, protected by a single password from ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env using an httpOnly session cookie. No user table, no OAuth.
- Kanban board per job with stages: applied, screening, interview, offer, hired, rejected. Drag and drop, or simple stage buttons if drag is fragile.
- Candidate drawer: details, resume download link, notes with timestamps, stage history.
- Three editable email templates (received, invite to interview, rejection) with {{name}} and {{job}} substitution, sent via nodemailer using SMTP creds from .env. Log every send.
- Job editor: create, edit, open/close.
- CSV export of candidates per job.
- A "delete candidate" action that removes the row and the resume file, and a nightly-ish script that purges candidates older than RETENTION_DAYS.

Explicitly out of scope: job board syndication, LinkedIn or Indeed posting, calendar and interview scheduling, multi-user accounts and permissions, scorecards, resume parsing, analytics, telemetry.

Ship a seed script with two jobs and five fake candidates, a README with setup steps, and .env.example listing ADMIN_PASSWORD, SMTP_URL, FROM_EMAIL, RETENTION_DAYS. Keep it one repo, no Docker.
